result:
An invitation is created from the members settings page, stored as a hashed token plus an email and a role, and turned into a membership only when a signed-in user posts that raw token back. The issuing path never puts the raw token into an email.

## Before the row exists

The page is `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx`. `loadTenantContext` calls `getActor`, which reads the session with `getSessionPrincipal` and then `resolveActorForOrg`. That lookup requires a live membership (`status` `active`, not archived) in the organization named by the slug. `can(actor, "member:read", …)` in `src/lib/permissions.ts` must allow the page; otherwise it `notFound()`s. `member:read` is granted from `viewer` up.

The invite form is rendered only when `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` is true. The role matrix maps `member:invite` to `admin`, so the actor’s `ROLE_RANK` must be admin or owner. The page also calls `checkLimit(org.id, "seats")` in `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`. That reads the subscription’s plan (the `organizations.plan` column only if there is no subscription) and `organization_usage.seatsUsed`.

`InviteMemberForm` (`src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx`) runs `can` again against `organizationResource` and hides itself when that fails. It calls `getPlanLimits` and disables the email field and the button when `seatCheck.exceeded` or `remaining <= 0`. `RoleSelect.assignableRoles` enables only roles for which `hasRoleAtLeast(actor.role, role)` is true. On submit the form parses `inviteMemberSchema` from `src/schemas/member.ts`: `emailSchema` (an email, max 254 characters, lowercased), `invitableRoleSchema` (`admin`, `member`, or `viewer`; `owner` fails), and an optional `message` of at most 500 characters. The message is never read again.

`inviteMemberAction` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` goes through `withAction`:

1. `inviteMemberSchema` is parsed again.
2. `requireActorFor(orgId)` requires a session whose `activeOrgId` is set, an organization that exists, an active membership, and `assertOrgScope`.
3. `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` runs with a placeholder member id (`PENDING_MEMBER_ID`) and `targetRole` set to the requested role. The decision is still the role matrix; the target role does not add a second rule.
4. `consumeRateLimit(orgId, "member:invite")` spends one token. The bucket in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` starts at capacity 20 and refills 2 per minute, then scales with the plan’s `apiRequestsPerHour / 100`.
5. `getOrganizationSummary` loads `usage.seatsUsed`. If `seatsUsed + 1` is greater than `getPlanLimits(organization.plan).seats`, the action throws `PlanLimitError`. This plan is the organization row’s plan, and this counter is the usage cache of active members.
6. `inviteMember` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` forwards a one-item batch to `inviteMembers`.

`inviteMembers` checks again, in this order:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)`.
2. `assertCan(actor, "member:invite", orgResource(input.orgId))`.
3. `consumeRateLimit` a second time, with a cost equal to the batch length. One invite from the settings page therefore spends two tokens.
4. `findOrgById`.
5. Seats taken equals `countActiveMembers` (status `active`, not archived) plus `countPendingInvitations`. Pending means `acceptedAt` and `revokedAt` are both null. Expired rows are included.
6. `wouldExceedLimit(org.plan, "seats", seatsUsed, batchLength)` from `src/config/plan-limits.ts`. The ceilings are 3 (free), 10 (starter), 50 (growth), and unlimited (enterprise). A batch that does not fit is rejected as a whole, before any insert.

There is no lookup of an existing user, an existing member with that email, or an outstanding invite for that email. The `(org_id, email)` index is not unique, so a second invite to the same address is another pending row and another seat in this count.

## What is stored, and what the link would have to carry

For each invite, `randomToken(32)` draws 32 bytes and encodes them as base64url. `hashToken` is SHA-256 hex. `insertInvitation` in `src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts` writes the `invitations` table: a new ULID, `org_id`, the lowercased email, the role, `invited_by` (the actor’s user id), `token_hash`, `expires_at` (now plus `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS`, which is 14), and null `accepted_at` and `revoked_at`. `token_hash` has a unique index. `toInvitation` copies that hash into the domain field `Invitation.token`, and that object is what `inviteMemberAction` returns. The raw token is not a column.

`emit("member.invited", …)` publishes `orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt` (the row’s `createdAt`), `email`, and `role`. The payload type in `src/types/event.ts` has no token field. With handlers registered from `src/instrumentation.ts` through `registerEventHandlers`, `registerActivityListeners` in `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` writes one audit row: action `member.invited`, subject kind `member`, subject id the email, summary `Invited ${email} as ${role}`. No other subscriber handles `member.invited`. The usage cache does not move, and `notify` is not called. `inviteMemberAction` then revalidates the tags `org:${orgId}`, `members`, and `invitations`.

The raw token is a local variable inside the loop. After `hashToken(token)` it is dropped. `InviteMemberForm` only clears the email box on success. `InviteEmail` in `src/emails/invite-email.tsx` is built to show the inviter’s name, the organization name, `humanizeRole(role)`, the expiry, and a button whose `href` is `acceptUrl`. `renderTemplate("invite")` in `src/emails/render.ts` can render that component. `inviteMember`, `inviteMembers`, and the `member.invited` handler never call `renderTemplate`, `renderEmail`, or `sendEmail`. `sendEmail` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` only logs a draft. So a successful invite leaves a hash in the database and an activity row, and it does not produce a message.

The accept route that a link would have to hit is `/invite/<raw token>`, implemented by `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`. That page also reads an optional `org` query string and passes it to the form as `orgSlug`. Nothing in the issuer builds that URL. `src/lib/url.ts` has no invite helper. `resendInvitation` revokes the old row and calls `inviteMember` again, which mints a new raw token and again discards it. The pending-invitations page wires revoke and does not wire resend.

## When the link is opened

`src/proxy.ts` lists `/invite` as public, so a missing session cookie does not bounce the request. The page then does its own checks, and it never looks the token up:

1. `invitationTokenSchema` in `src/schemas/invitation.ts` requires length 32–128 and the alphabet `A-Za-z0-9_-`. A bad shape renders “This invitation is not valid” and stops.
2. `getSessionPrincipal()` must return a principal. Otherwise the page redirects to `/login?next=/invite/${token}`.
3. `safeDestination` on the login page keeps a `next` value only when it is a same-site path. After `loginAction` sets the session cookie, `LoginForm` navigates there. A visitor who is already signed in is redirected there immediately. `register` in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts` creates a new user and a new workspace through `createOrganization`. The invite page never sends the visitor to register, and acceptance never creates a user. The colleague has to already have an account and a session.
4. With a session, `InviteAcceptForm` posts `{ token }` to `acceptInvitationAction`.

`acceptInvitationAction` in `src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts` stays outside `withAction`, because there is no membership to turn into an `Actor` yet:

1. `acceptInvitationTokenSchema` parses the token again.
2. `getSessionPrincipal()` throws `UnauthorizedActionError` when it is missing.
3. `acceptInvitation(principal.userId, { token })` runs.
4. `assertSeatAvailable` runs after that returns.

`acceptInvitation` treats the token as the credential:

1. `findInvitationByTokenHash(hashToken(input.token))`. This is the one repository read that is not scoped by `orgId`; the hash carries the tenant. A miss throws from `requireFound`.
2. A non-null `revokedAt` throws “revoked”.
3. A non-null `acceptedAt` throws “already been accepted”.
4. `expiresAt <=` the current ISO timestamp throws “expired”. Equality counts as expired. The window is the 14 days stored at insert.
5. `findMember(invitation.orgId, userId)` returns an existing live membership immediately. In that case the invitation stays pending (`acceptedAt` remains null, so `countPendingInvitations` still counts it) and `member.joined` is not emitted.
6. Otherwise `insertMember` writes `members`: a new id, the invitation’s `orgId`, the session user id, the invitation’s role, status `active`, `invitedBy` from the invitation, `joinedAt` now, `lastSeenAt` null. `(org_id, user_id)` is unique.
7. `markInvitationAccepted` sets `acceptedAt`.
8. `emit("member.joined", …)` publishes `orgId`, `actorId` equal to the joining user id, `memberId`, `userId`, and `role`.

The stored email is not compared with `principal.email`. The session user who presents the raw token receives the invitation’s role. The service does not re-check the seat quota or the rate limit.

`assertSeatAvailable` then calls `resolveActor`, which now succeeds, and `getOrganizationSummary`, which requires `org:read` (viewer and above) and reads `usage.seatsUsed`. `emit` waits for handlers, so the usage listener has already added one seat when that read happens. If `seatsUsed` is greater than `getPlanLimits(organization.plan).seats`, the action returns `PlanLimitError`. The form shows the out-of-seats message and does not navigate. The member row, `acceptedAt`, the usage increment, and the join notification are already written. A second click hits the “already accepted” check.

On success the form navigates to `/${orgSlug}` when the link included `?org=`, and to `/orgs` otherwise.

## What the rest of the system learns

`registerEventHandlers` attaches the listeners. On `member.joined`:

- `registerUsageListeners` calls `incrementUsage(orgId, { seatsUsed: 1 })` on `organization_usage`. Pending invites were never in that cache; they only affected the live count inside `inviteMembers`. Later, `runUsageRollupJob` calls `recomputeUsage`, which recounts active, non-archived members and rewrites the cache. That recount also ignores pending invitations.
- The notification fan-out in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`, loaded because `event-registry` imports it, calls `notify(orgId, "member_joined", [org.ownerId], …)`. The owner is skipped when the owner is the person who joined, because `notify` drops a recipient equal to `actorId`. With no stored preference the channels are `in_app` and `email`, and those are columns on the notification row: title “A new member joined”, a body containing the user id and role, and `href` `/settings/members`. `notify` inserts rows. It does not call `sendEmail`. `runDigestEmailJob` will include the row only for users who set `digestOnly`, and only when the `digest_email` flag is on for the plan.

`registerActivityListeners` does not subscribe to `member.joined`, so the audit log keeps the earlier “invited” row and does not gain a “joined” row from this event. `registerWebhookListeners` forwards issue, comment, and billing events. `member.joined` is a value in `webhookEventTypeSchema`, and it is not one of those subscriptions. The search listeners ignore both member events.

Acceptance does not change `sessions.active_org_id`. Membership is what later requests use. `listOrgsForUser` joins live `members` rows to organizations, so `/orgs` lists the workspace and redirects into it when it is the user’s only organization. The tenant layout `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx` calls `resolveActorForOrg` again: organization by slug, active membership, an `Actor` whose `role` is the role copied from the invitation, `assertOrgScope`, and `touchLastSeen`. From that request on, `can()` uses that role. The members and invitations pages are `force-dynamic`, so the next load sees the new member and an invitation that `InvitationList.isPending` no longer treats as pending.
